The manuscript says: “We use Theorem 2.1 in the formulation of [8, Theorem 2.3], with the normalization and matrix-extension conventions fixed at the start of its Section 2.” Its bibliography: “[8] Henning Olai Milhøj and Mikael Rørdam, Around traces and quasitraces, preprint, 2023, version 2, 30 November 2023; to appear in Münster J. scope: Theorem 2.1 (Quasitrace existence) of the manuscript “A counterexample to Kaplansky's quasitrace conjecture and failure of tensor-product stable finiteness” (preprints/A-counterexample-to-Kaplanskys-quasitrace-conjecture-September-23-2026/paper.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 294 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 c46465adfaef9b9f), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 4. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. The manuscript presents this as a result of other work, which it uses; the attribution names that work in the manuscript's own words. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: A unital C∗-algebra C admits a normalized 2- quasitrace if and only if Mm(C) is not properly infinite for every positive integer m.
